conversations.subject: Account security alert - multiple failed login attempts

comments.author: customer
comments.content: I just received multiple email notifications about failed login attempts to my admin account over the past hour. I'm concerned my account might be under attack. I wasn't trying to log in during this time, and the IP addresses in the alerts are not from our company. Can you help me secure my account and investigate what's happening?

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
I understand your concern about the security alerts, and you're right to reach out immediately. Account security is our top priority, and we'll help you address this right away.

First, let's secure your account:

1. I've temporarily locked your account to prevent unauthorized access
2. I've sent a password reset link to your alternate email (ending in @gmail.com)
3. Please change your password immediately using that link

Once you've reset your password, please enable two-factor authentication if you haven't already. I can guide you through that process.

Regarding the login attempts, I can see 17 failed attempts from 3 different IP addresses. None were successful, and our security system automatically blocked further attempts after the 10th failure. Would you like me to share more details about these attempts?

comments.author: customer
comments.content: Thank you for acting quickly. I've reset my password using the link you sent. Please do share more details about those login attempts - where were they coming from? And yes, I'd like to set up two-factor authentication. I thought it was already enabled, but maybe not on this particular account.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
I'm glad you've reset your password. Here are the details of the login attempts:

- 8 attempts from IP 185.176.xx.xx (located in Russia)
- 6 attempts from IP 103.43.xx.xx (located in China)
- 3 attempts from IP 91.134.xx.xx (located in Romania)

These appear to be automated attempts rather than targeted attacks, as they followed common brute force patterns. Our systems blocked them appropriately, and no data was compromised.

For two-factor authentication, please follow these steps:

1. Go to Account Settings > Security
2. Click "Enable Two-Factor Authentication"
3. Choose your preferred method (app or SMS)
4. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete setup

Once you've done this, I recommend reviewing all admin accounts in your organization to ensure they all have 2FA enabled. Would you like me to help you run a security audit to identify any other accounts that may need additional protection?

comments.author: customer
comments.content: I've enabled 2FA using Google Authenticator. Those IP addresses are definitely concerning - none of our team members are in those countries. A security audit sounds like a good idea. Can you help with that and also let me know if there's a way to restrict login attempts to only come from approved countries or IP ranges? We're a US-based company and don't have any international operations.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Great job enabling 2FA! I'm running the security audit now and will share the results shortly.

Regarding geographic restrictions, yes, we do offer IP and location-based restrictions. Here's how to set them up:

1. Go to Admin Console > Security Settings > Access Controls
2. Enable "Geographic Restrictions"
3. Select "United States" or add specific countries you want to allow
4. You can also add specific IP ranges to allow in the "IP Allowlist" section

This will block any login attempts from outside your approved locations. I recommend setting this up at the organization level rather than individual accounts for consistent protection.

The security audit is complete, and I've found that 3 of your 7 admin accounts don't have 2FA enabled. Would you like me to send password reset requests to those users with instructions to enable 2FA when they create their new passwords?

comments.author: customer
comments.content: Yes, please send those reset requests to the other admins. I just set up the geographic restriction to only allow logins from the US, and I've added our office IP ranges to the allowlist. Would you recommend any other security measures we should implement? This incident has made me realize we need to be more proactive about our account security.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
I've sent the password reset requests with 2FA instructions to the other admin users. They'll receive emails shortly.

You've already taken excellent steps to secure your account, but here are a few additional security measures I recommend:

1. Enable "Suspicious Activity Monitoring" (Admin Console > Security > Advanced) - This uses machine learning to detect unusual patterns even within allowed regions

2. Set up "Session Timeout" to automatically log users out after a period of inactivity (recommend 30-60 minutes)

3. Enable "Login History Alerts" to get notifications of successful logins to admin accounts

4. Schedule a monthly security report to be emailed to you, showing login patterns and potential issues

I can help you configure any of these options now, or provide documentation for your team to implement them. Would you like me to enable any of these features for your account right away?

conversations.subject: Data export fails with timeout error

comments.author: customer
comments.content: For the past week, I've been trying to export our quarterly analytics data but keep getting a timeout error. The export starts, runs for about 5 minutes, then fails with the message: "Export timed out - please try again with a smaller data set". This worked fine last quarter with a similar amount of data. We need this export for our board meeting next week, so it's becoming urgent.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
I'm sorry to hear you're experiencing issues with the data export feature. Timeout errors like this can be frustrating, especially when you have an upcoming board meeting.

To help troubleshoot this issue, could you please provide a few more details:

1. Approximately how many records are you trying to export?
2. Are you including any custom metrics or calculated fields in this export?
3. What file format are you exporting to (CSV, Excel, etc.)?
4. Have you tried breaking the export into smaller date ranges?

With this information, I'll be able to better understand what might be causing the timeout and suggest the most effective solution.

comments.author: customer
comments.content: We're trying to export about 1.2 million records with standard fields (no custom calculations). We're exporting to CSV format. I tried breaking it down into monthly exports instead of quarterly, but even the monthly exports are failing now. It seems like the system has gotten slower compared to three months ago when we did our last export. Is there a system issue happening?

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Thank you for providing those details. You're right to question if something has changed in our system since your last successful export.

After checking our system status and recent updates, I can confirm that we deployed an upgrade to our analytics engine two weeks ago. While this improved performance for most queries, we've identified an issue affecting large data exports, which matches what you're experiencing.

I have two options to help you get your data for the board meeting:

1. Immediate workaround: I can set up a scheduled export that will run during off-peak hours and automatically email you the results. This uses a different export process that isn't affected by the timeout issue.

2. Backend export: Our technical team can extract the data directly from the database for you within 24-48 hours.

Which option would you prefer? Also, we're deploying a fix for this issue this weekend, but I understand that doesn't help with your immediate need for the board meeting.

comments.author: customer
comments.content: The scheduled export sounds like the best option if it can be completed quickly. When would it run and how soon could I get the data? If it takes more than 24 hours, the backend export might be better. Our board meeting is on Wednesday morning, so I need this data by Tuesday at the latest for preparation.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
I completely understand your timeline constraints. The scheduled export can be set up to run tonight at 10 PM when system usage is lower, and you would receive the data by email tomorrow morning. This should comfortably meet your Tuesday deadline.

I've gone ahead and configured the scheduled export with the following settings:
- Full quarterly data (all 1.2 million records)
- CSV format as requested
- Will run at 10 PM tonight
- Results will be emailed to your registered email address

The export has been prioritized in our system to ensure it completes successfully. You'll receive a confirmation email when the export begins and another when it's complete with the data attached.

Would you like me to add any other email addresses to receive the export results? Also, is there anything specific about the data formatting that you need for your board presentation?

comments.author: customer
comments.content:
That schedule works perfectly. Please also send the export to my colleague alex@ourcompany.com as she's helping prepare the presentation. The standard data formatting is fine - we'll be processing it further on our end anyway.

Do you think the upcoming fix will prevent this issue for our next quarterly export? It's a bit concerning that we're having to use workarounds for what used to be a straightforward process.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
I've added alex@ourcompany.com to receive the export results as well.

Regarding your concern about future exports: Yes, the fix being deployed this weekend (version 4.5.3) specifically addresses this timeout issue for large data exports. Our engineering team has already tested exports of up to 5 million records without timeouts, so your quarterly export should work smoothly going forward.

I completely understand your concern about needing workarounds for what should be a basic function. As a goodwill gesture, I've also arranged for your account to be automatically included in our beta testing group for the new export engine being released next month. This will give you access to significantly faster exports and new formatting options before they're generally available.

After your board meeting, I'd appreciate any feedback on the scheduled export process so we can continue to improve our system. Is there anything else you need assistance with regarding the data export?

comments.author: customer
comments.content: Thank you! The scheduled export worked perfectly - both Alex and I received the full data set this morning. I appreciate you finding a solution so quickly and including us in the beta for the new export engine. That's a nice bonus. I'll be sure to provide feedback after we've had a chance to review everything. This issue has been resolved to my satisfaction.

conversations.subject: Mobile app crashes when submitting forms

comments.author: customer
comments.content: Your mobile app keeps crashing whenever I try to submit any form. I've tried uninstalling and reinstalling the app, clearing cache, and even using a different device, but the problem persists. This started happening after I updated to the newest version yesterday. Our field teams rely on this app to submit reports, and this is severely impacting our operations. Please fix this immediately!

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
I'm very sorry to hear about the crashing issues you're experiencing with our mobile app. This is clearly disrupting your operations, and we'll work urgently to resolve it.

To help us diagnose the specific cause, could you please provide a few additional details:

1. What type of device and OS version are you using (e.g., iPhone 13 with iOS 16.5)?
2. What version of our app did you update to?
3. Are there any specific form fields (like image uploads or location data) that seem to trigger the crash?
4. Does the app crash immediately when tapping submit, or after a loading period?

In the meantime, as a temporary workaround, you can access the web version of our platform through your mobile browser, which should allow your field teams to submit reports while we investigate the app issue.

comments.author: customer
comments.content:
We're using various iPhone models (mostly iPhone 12 and 13) with iOS 16.4 and 16.5. The app version is 5.1.8 according to the App Store. The crashes happen immediately after tapping submit on ANY form - it doesn't seem to matter what fields are filled out. Even the simplest forms with just text fields crash.

The web version workaround isn't practical for our field teams. They're often in areas with poor connectivity, and the app is supposed to work offline and sync when connection is restored. The web version requires constant connection. We need the app fixed ASAP or we need a way to roll back to the previous version that was working.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Thank you for those details. You're right that the web version isn't a good solution for teams with connectivity challenges.

After checking our crash reports and your specific information, we've identified the issue. There's a bug in version 5.1.8 that affects the form submission process when offline mode is enabled, which explains why it's happening across all forms and devices.

I have two immediate solutions to offer:

1. Rollback option: You can download version 5.1.7 from our support portal here: [secure-link-to-previous-version]. This is not available through the App Store but can be distributed to your team through your MDM system if you have one.

2. Fix option: Our development team has already created a patch (version 5.1.9) that fixes this issue. It's currently in expedited review with Apple and should be available within 24 hours. We can add you to the TestFlight program to get immediate access before the App Store approval if you prefer.

Which option would work better for your team? Also, I've marked this as a high-priority issue affecting multiple customers, so our product team is fully aware of the impact.

comments.author: customer
comments.content:
Let's do both. We'll use the rollback version 5.1.7 immediately to get our teams operational again, and then update to 5.1.9 once it's available. Please add us to the TestFlight program as well so we can verify that the fix works before rolling it out to everyone.

I'm still frustrated that such a critical bug made it through your testing process. Our teams lost almost a full day of proper reporting. Will there be any changes to your QA process to prevent similar issues in the future?

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
I've sent you the link to download version 5.1.7 via a secure email, and I've also added your account to our TestFlight program. You should receive an invitation email within the next 15 minutes with instructions to access the 5.1.9 beta version.

Your frustration is completely valid. This bug should absolutely have been caught before release, and I apologize for the disruption it caused to your operations. In response to this incident, our QA team is implementing three specific changes:

1. Expanded offline mode testing protocol - All future releases will undergo specific testing scenarios mimicking poor connectivity conditions

2. Beta program expansion - We're creating a dedicated "Field Operations" beta testing group to ensure companies like yours can optionally test new versions before they're widely released

3. Staged rollouts - Starting with version 5.2, we'll roll out updates to 10% of users first, monitor for issues, then continue the rollout gradually

I'd also like to offer you two months of service credit as compensation for the operational disruption. While this doesn't make up for the lost productivity, we want to acknowledge the impact this had on your business.

comments.author: customer
comments.content:
Thank you for the quick response and solutions. We've started distributing version 5.1.7 to our teams, and I've received the TestFlight invitation. The service credit is appreciated, though as you noted, it doesn't fully address the lost time. 

The QA process changes sound good, especially the Field Operations beta group. Please add us to that group when it's available - we'd rather catch these issues before they impact our operations. For now, I'll consider this issue on the way to resolution, and will follow up once we've verified the fix in 5.1.9.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
You're welcome, and I've noted your interest in joining the Field Operations beta group. I'll make sure you're added as soon as it's established, which should be within the next two weeks.

I completely understand that this issue isn't fully resolved until you've verified the fix works for your team. I'll keep this ticket open and active until we get confirmation that version 5.1.9 is working properly for you.

The TestFlight version is available now, and the public App Store update has been submitted with an expedited review request. I'll send you another update tomorrow with the status of the App Store release, or sooner if it becomes available.

Please don't hesitate to reach out if you encounter any other issues with version 5.1.7 in the meantime, or if you have any feedback after testing the 5.1.9 beta version.

comments.author: customer
comments.content: Good news - we've tested the 5.1.9 TestFlight version and it resolves the crashing issue. Forms are submitting correctly, including in offline mode. Once this version is in the App Store, we'll upgrade our entire team. Thanks for the quick turnaround on the fix. I still hope to see more rigorous testing in the future, but I appreciate how responsive you've been in addressing the problem.

conversations.subject: Need to add users in bulk to our enterprise account

comments.author: customer
comments.content: Our company just acquired another business, and I need to add about 250 new users to our enterprise account. I don't see any way to do this in bulk from the admin dashboard. Is there a way to upload a CSV file or something similar? Manually adding this many users would take hours, and we need to get them onboarded by next week.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Welcome to your expanded team! I'd be happy to help you add those 250 new users efficiently.

Yes, we do offer bulk user imports for Enterprise accounts. There are three ways you can do this:

1. CSV Upload: You can prepare a CSV file with user details and upload it through Admin Dashboard > Users > Import

2. SCIM Provisioning: If you use Azure AD, Okta, or OneLogin, you can set up automatic user provisioning

3. API Integration: For a more customized approach, you can use our User Management API

The quickest option for your timeline would be the CSV upload. Would you like me to provide you with the template and instructions for this method? Or would you prefer information about one of the other approaches?

comments.author: customer
comments.content: The CSV upload sounds like the best option for our immediate needs. Please send me the template and instructions. Also, could you clarify what happens with licensing? We have 300 licenses currently and are adding 250 users - will the system automatically add the additional licenses to our account and bill us, or do we need to purchase them separately first?

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
I've attached the CSV template to this message. Here's a quick overview of the process:

1. Fill in the required fields (email, first name, last name) and any optional fields you want to pre-configure
2. Save as a CSV file
3. Go to Admin Dashboard > Users > Import
4. Upload your file and follow the validation steps
5. Confirm the import

Regarding licensing: As an Enterprise customer, you have flexible licensing enabled, which means you can add users at any time and the additional licenses will be automatically provisioned. The additional 250 licenses will be pro-rated for the remainder of your current billing cycle.

You'll see the updated license count and charges on your next invoice. There's no need to purchase anything separately or contact the billing department first.

Would you like me to walk you through the import process with a screen sharing session, or do you feel comfortable proceeding with the instructions?

comments.author: customer
comments.content: Thanks for the template and clarification on the licensing. I think I can handle the import process with the instructions you provided. One more question though - these new users will need to be assigned to different teams/projects based on their departments. Does the CSV template have a column for team assignment, or do we need to organize them after the import?

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Great question! Yes, the CSV template does support team assignments. In the template I sent, you'll find columns for:

- team_name: Enter the exact name of an existing team
- role_name: Specify their role within that team (Viewer, Editor, Admin, etc.)
- department: For organizational grouping

You can assign users to multiple teams by using a pipe symbol (|) as a separator, like this:
"Team A|Team B|Team C" in the team_name column and "Editor|Viewer|Admin" in the role_name column (matching the order of teams).

If you're creating new teams specifically for these users, I recommend setting those up before doing the import. Alternatively, you can import the users first and then use our bulk assignment tool (Admin Dashboard > Teams > Manage > Add Members) to organize them afterward.

Do you already have the teams created, or would you like information on bulk-creating teams as well?

comments.author: customer
comments.content: This is perfect. We already have the teams created, so I'll use the pipe symbol method to assign everyone appropriately. I'm going to prepare the CSV file today and plan to do the import tomorrow morning. If I run into any issues, I'll let you know. Thanks for your help!

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
You're very welcome! That sounds like a great plan to prepare the CSV today and perform the import tomorrow morning. 

As a best practice, I recommend importing a small test batch first (maybe 5-10 users) to verify everything works as expected before proceeding with the full list. This can save time troubleshooting if there are any formatting issues.

I've added a note to your account about this planned bulk import. Our system monitoring team will be aware of the large user addition to ensure it processes smoothly.

Feel free to reach out if you have any questions while preparing the CSV or during the import process. I'll be happy to help! Good luck with onboarding your new team members.

comments.author: customer
comments.content: Update: I completed the import this morning and it worked flawlessly! All 250 users were added with the correct team assignments. The system sent welcome emails automatically, and we're already seeing new users logging in. Thanks again for your help with this - you saved us a tremendous amount of time.
